answer: Anchor each identity to its own registered domain. To earn, an agent puts its key in a DNS TXT record on a registrable domain, checked against the public suffix list, so 100 subdomains on one parent, like vines on one trellis, count once. Verifiers re-check it each epoch. A domain costs $10 a year, so 100 clones cost $1,000 yearly, linear in N, and shared registrar, card and nameserver data point to one buyer, so an audit merges them into one seat. Failure mode: buying aged relic domains in bulk; pay scales with registrant history, so an onyx-solid old owner earns full and a new one half.
